title: rhus viridiflora var. canadensis
intro: Rhus viridiflora var. canadensis, commonly known as poison sumac, is a plant native to eastern North America. It is known for its health benefits, particularly in traditional medicine, where it has been used to treat conditions such as fever, rheumatism, and skin irritations due to its anti-inflammatory and antiseptic properties. The therapeutic actions of poison sumac include reducing inflammation and pain, as well as exhibiting antimicrobial and antioxidant activities. The bioactive constituents of the plant include flavonoids, alkaloids, and triterpenoids, which contribute to its medicinal properties.
